# evcc

> evcc is open-source energy management for your home. It charges your electric car with solar surplus or in the cheapest hours of a dynamic tariff and also controls heat pumps, switchable sockets and home batteries. It runs locally on your own hardware and works with hundreds of chargers, meters and vehicles.

The documentation lives on docs.evcc.io. Every docs page is also available as markdown by appending .md to its URL.

## Documentation

- [Documentation index](https://docs.evcc.io/llms.txt): every docs page with a one-line summary and a link to its markdown version
- [Getting started](https://docs.evcc.io/en/installation.md): all ways to install evcc, from the Raspberry Pi image to Docker, Home Assistant, Linux, macOS and Windows
- [Features](https://docs.evcc.io/llms-features.txt): solar surplus charging, dynamic tariffs, charging plans, home battery, load management
- [Supported devices](https://docs.evcc.io/llms-devices.txt): every supported charger, meter, vehicle and tariff
- [Integrations](https://docs.evcc.io/llms-integrations.txt): MQTT and REST APIs, MCP server, Home Assistant and other smart home systems

## Project

- [Source code](https://github.com/evcc-io/evcc): MIT licensed
- [Sponsorship](https://docs.evcc.io/en/sponsorship.md): why some chargers need a sponsor token and how to get one
- [Media kit](https://evcc.io/en/media-kit/): logos, screenshots and app icons
